h1: Wanarom Residence Hotel — a stay near Krabi Airport with clean rooms, peace and quiet, and great value
intro: If your flight lands in Krabi late at night, or you have to fly out before dawn and would rather not risk a long drive — Wanarom Residence Hotel is a name that comes up often among stays near Krabi Airport · It's a small 2-star property on Petchkasem Road in the Krabi Noi area, open since 2018, with around 53 rooms, most with a small balcony plus air conditioning, a TV, a fridge, and an en-suite bathroom · What guests consistently mention is that it's only about 5.5 km or an 8-minute drive from Krabi Airport (KBV), next to a 7-Eleven and a Lotus's, with rooms many call cleaner and more spacious than expected at this price · Rated 8.9 from 144 reviews on Trip.com (cleanliness as high as 9.3) and 4.9 out of 5 on TripAdvisor · From about THB 850/night.

body.html: Who Wanarom Residence Hotel is right for — To put it as briefly as possible, Wanarom Residence Hotel is a stay for people who care more about "being close to the airport and having a clean room" than about a resort atmosphere or sea views · It's not a beachfront stay where you wake up and walk straight to the water, and it's not a downtown spot where you can stroll to the night market or walking street. Instead, it's a small 2-star property in the Krabi Noi area on Petchkasem Road, the main route linking Krabi Airport with the town · Open since 2018, it still counts as a fairly new building compared with many budget stays in Krabi, with around 53 rooms run as a small, hands-on operation rather than part of a big hotel chain · Real reviews on both Trip.com and TripAdvisor agree that the people it suits are travellers landing on a late flight or flying out before dawn, those using Krabi as a stopover before heading to Koh Lanta, Tubkaak, or Phang Nga, people driving their own car who want free parking, and budget travellers who want a clean room without spending much · On the flip side, those likely to be disappointed are people expecting a relaxing seaside vibe, a swimming pool, or being able to walk straight out to eat, because it sits outside the main tourist areas and you need a car to get around · Put another way, Wanarom plays the "clean, well-priced stay near the airport" angle well in the few-hundred to low-thousand baht range — which is exactly what the 8.9 rating from 144 reviews confirms: people who arrive with expectations that match what the place actually is leave satisfied.

Location and getting around — This is undeniably Wanarom Residence Hotel's number-one selling point · The property sits at 351 Moo 12 Petchkasem Road, Krabi Noi, Mueang Krabi, on the main route between the airport and the town · What reviews mention most is that it's only about 5.5 km or roughly an 8-minute drive from Krabi Airport (KBV), so anyone landing on a late flight or checking in for an early-morning departure doesn't have to sit in the car for long or risk traffic · Around the property there's a 7-Eleven right next door and a Lotus's (formerly Tesco Lotus) nearby, so basic food and supplies are easy to find even though it's not central · As for sights, you can reach a few, such as Wat Tham Suea (Tiger Cave Temple) about 8–10 minutes away by car and the Pak Nam area of Krabi town in around 10–15 minutes · If you want to go further, Ao Nang Beach is about 30–40 minutes by car, and the piers for the islands are a short drive from the town · The honest caveat to mention is that this location "isn't a walkable area" — it's surrounded by a main road and residential land, with few restaurants or cafés to wander to, and many reviews stress that you pretty much need a car or have to call a Grab/taxi every time you head out, since there's no motorbike rental nearby · For people who understand they're paying for "closeness to the airport and quiet" rather than "walk-out convenience," this location does the job well.

"Landed in the evening, called a car and was there in no time. The room was very clean and bigger than I expected, and that night I slept soundly in total silence. In the morning it was under ten minutes' drive to the airport — for a transit night before a connecting flight, this place is the real deal at a very light price."

Room types and decor — Wanarom Residence Hotel has around 53 rooms, split into a few types to suit your group size and budget · The main ones are the Deluxe Double Room, with one large bed, ideal for a solo traveller or couple, and the Standard / Twin Room, set up with two single beds or, in some rooms, both a single and a queen, ideal for friends or a small family who want separate beds · Most rooms have a small balcony looking out over the garden or a corner of the town, where you can sit and catch the breeze or hang laundry after a day out · The decor is a simple modern style in white and cream, set against light wood and a polished tile floor that's easy to keep clean, with beds made up in clean white linen and towels often folded into a welcoming swan shape · The point many reviews emphasise is that the rooms are very clean and more spacious than expected at this price, with the cleanliness score on Trip.com as high as 9.3, which is very high for a 2-star stay · Every room has air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a fridge, a safe, free drinking water, and an en-suite bathroom with a water heater and a shower that many praise for good water pressure · To be straight about it, some reviews do note details in the room, such as a bed that's quite firm for some people, few places to hang towels, or a fridge in some rooms that doesn't work all that well · If you need a soft mattress, set your expectations accordingly, and if you want an especially quiet room, ask for one that doesn't face the main road when you book.

Facilities and extra services — Set your expectations from the start that Wanarom Residence Hotel is a small 2-star stay: there's no swimming pool, and no full gym or spa · But what you really need is all there and done well · The clear advantage is free private parking on-site, which matters a lot for people renting a car to tour Krabi themselves, since parking in tourist areas and the town centre is hard to find and often comes with a charge · There's free Wi-Fi in the common areas (some reviews say the signal is a bit weaker in certain spots in the rooms, so if you need to work online, plan ahead or bring a backup data SIM) · There's an on-site restaurant serving simple food, plus free coffee, which helps a lot in an area with no nearby places to walk to · There's laundry service, and a garden and terrace to sit out in, plus a front desk that helps arrange tours, book transfers, and suggest routes · As for airport transfers, they're available but worth asking about and booking ahead, because the information differs across platforms — some say it's offered, others say you have to request it first · A few reviews note that the team isn't able to arrange a pickup from the pier, so if you need a transfer to a specific point, check clearly before you book · Overall, the facilities here are "in line with the price and the role of a stay near the airport" — no fancy frills, but covering what someone on a transit night actually needs.

Food and nearby eateries — Wanarom Residence Hotel has an on-site restaurant serving simple food, plus free coffee, which many reviews see as a plus for a stay outside the restaurant district · On breakfast, the honest truth is that the information differs across platforms — at some points there's a breakfast service, at others it's not included in the room rate, so always check the terms with the property or the platform you book through · What helps offset the food limitations is the location, next to a 7-Eleven and close to a Lotus's, so basic food and supplies are easy to find, even without street-side restaurants to stroll past like in town · For people who drive their own car or call a Grab, heading out to eat in Krabi town, about 10–15 minutes away, is no trouble, since the town has plenty of night markets, seafood spots, and southern-Thai restaurants at local prices · Simply put, if you're after a stroll-and-snack vibe around the property, this isn't the spot — but if you're willing to drive or take a short ride into town, food isn't a problem · Many people therefore stock up on snacks from 7-Eleven or Lotus's for late-night and early-morning meals, then head out for their main meals in town or in the tourist area they're aiming for.

Service and guest care — Service is another point that earns consistent praise in real reviews of Wanarom Residence Hotel, with the service score on Trip.com at around 8.8 · Because it's a small, family-run stay, several staff are described as friendly, helpful, and attentive · Many international reviews use the words "helpful" and "kind" repeatedly, especially about helping call a car to the airport, looking after people who arrive late, and advising on onward travel · For anyone landing on a late flight or having to wake before dawn to catch a plane, having a front desk that handles the car for you takes a lot of the stress out · To be straight about it, since it's a small property with a limited number of staff, there are stretches when no one is at the front desk and getting hold of someone may take a wait, and a few people feel the answers about certain transfer services come across as fairly blunt, even a touch curt · English communication may take a little patience at times, as at small stays generally · But overall, the goodwill and genuine care for guests is a strength that brings people back to leave positive reviews, with many saying they'll "definitely come back to stay again."

What real reviews say (both praise and criticism) — Drawing on Trip.com (rated 8.9 from 144 reviews · cleanliness 9.3, location 8.8, service 8.8, facilities 8.7) and TripAdvisor (4.9 out of 5), the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the rooms are very clean and bigger than expected (the most common compliment), the location is just about 8 minutes from the airport, it's peaceful and easy to sleep in, free parking, friendly and helpful staff, next to a 7-Eleven and close to a Lotus's, good water pressure, and free coffee · One review says "this is my second stay and I'll definitely be back," reflecting the satisfaction of repeat guests · On the critical side: the most-mentioned point is a bed that's quite firm for some people · Next come the basic facilities (such as some amenities provided in small quantities, no teaspoons, few towel hooks), a fridge that doesn't work well in some rooms, road noise from the main road in rooms facing the street, a location that requires a car to get around and is far from the main sights, and a few reviews that feel the rooms look slightly better in photos than in reality · These criticisms are common at budget stays near the airport, and most are solved by setting your expectations to match the price and the role of a "clean transit stay," rather than being big problems that would stop people recommending it.

"The room really was clean, the staff were lovely and helped call a car before dawn, and it's super close to the airport · The only downsides were the bed being a bit too firm for us, and having to call a car every time we went out because there's nothing to walk to nearby. Next time we have a connecting flight, we'll stay here again."

Price and value — Wanarom Residence Hotel's starting rate is around THB 850/night at normal prices (about 23–25 US dollars) and may climb to roughly THB 1,100–1,300 during high season or long weekends · Compared with similar-class stays in Krabi, what makes Wanarom feel good value among stays near the airport is its cleanliness score, as high as 9.3, and the fairly new building (opened 2018), which is cleaner and looks better than many older budget stays, plus the free parking and the peace and quiet · Compared with stays in Krabi town, like the Pak Nam area where you can walk to the market and the pier, Wanarom loses out on "walkability" but wins on "closeness to the airport and quiet" · And compared with the Ao Nang-side resorts that start at several times the price, this is cheaper on the room and suits nights when you didn't come to relax by the sea · But understand clearly that what you "don't" get is a pool, sea views, and a walkable location · If your trip is landing late and sleeping one night before catching a car to the islands, or packing up on your last night before an early flight, every baht you pay for closeness to the airport and a clean room earns its keep · But if you want to spend most of your time by a pool or on the beach, that same money is better put toward a beachfront resort.

What to know before you book — A few things help make the stay smoother · One, it's best suited to a transit night near the airport or the night before catching a car to the islands, not as a base for sightseeing; if your trip's goal is exploring the town or the beach, choose a stay in the Pak Nam area in town or on the Ao Nang side instead · Two, plan your transport well, because there's no motorbike rental or restaurants to walk to around the property — rent a car, be ready to call a Grab/taxi, or ask the property about transfer services in advance · Three, if you need a soft mattress, brace yourself for the bed, which many reviews call quite firm · Four, if quiet matters to you, ask for a room that doesn't face Petchkasem Road when you book, since there's some road noise from the main road · Five, check the breakfast and airport-transfer terms clearly before booking, because the information differs across platforms · Six, it's a small property, easy to book through OTAs like Agoda, Booking.com, or Trip.com — compare prices across a few and pick a free-cancellation option if your plans aren't firm yet · Seven, stock up on drinking water and snacks from the 7-Eleven next door for a late-night meal or before an early-morning flight.

The verdict — From all the real reviews, Wanarom Residence Hotel is the stay best suited to travellers wanting a clean, quiet, well-priced stay near Krabi Airport — whether landing on a late flight, flying out before dawn, or using it as a stopover before heading to Koh Lanta, Tubkaak, or Phang Nga · The 8.9 rating from 144 reviews, especially the cleanliness as high as 9.3, the still-new building (opened 2018), the free parking, and being just about 8 minutes from the airport, make it good value enough that it's hard to find a rival in the same role at this price · If you're after a resort atmosphere, sea views, a pool, or a walkable location, this isn't the answer, and you should look at stays on the Ao Nang side, Railay, or in the town instead · But for a trip that needs a clean night near the airport on an affordable budget, with helpful staff and the quiet to sleep your fill — Wanarom Residence Hotel fits that need squarely, which is why many people choose to stay here again every time they pass through Krabi.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Wanarom Residence Hotel Krabi

faq.q: Where is Wanarom Residence Hotel · how close is it to the airport?
faq.a: The property is at 351 Moo 12 Petchkasem Road, Krabi Noi, Mueang Krabi · It's only about 5.5 km or roughly an 8-minute drive from Krabi Airport (KBV) · It's next to a 7-Eleven and close to a Lotus's · Wat Tham Suea is about 8–10 minutes away, Krabi town about 10–15 minutes, and Ao Nang Beach about 30–40 minutes by car.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Wanarom Residence Hotel · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 850/night for a Deluxe Double Room at normal rates · There's a Standard / Twin room with two single beds for friends or a small family, and a Deluxe garden-view room that's quieter · It's easy to book through Agoda, Booking.com, or Trip.com — compare prices before booking · High-season rates (Nov–Feb) go up.

faq.q: Who is Wanarom Residence Hotel best suited for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for travellers wanting a clean, well-priced stay near Krabi Airport — whether landing on a late flight, flying out before dawn, or using it as a stopover before heading to Koh Lanta, Tubkaak, or Phang Nga · It suits people renting a car to tour themselves who want free parking · It's not for people who want to walk around the property, stay by the beach, or use a swimming pool.

faq.q: Does Wanarom Residence Hotel have a swimming pool and breakfast?
faq.a: There's no swimming pool, as it's a small 2-star stay near the airport · There's an on-site restaurant and free coffee, but the breakfast terms differ across platforms — at some points it's included, at others it's not in the room rate, so check before booking · There's free parking, free Wi-Fi in the common areas, laundry service, and a garden and terrace.

faq.q: Is Wanarom Residence Hotel noisy · which room should I ask for?
faq.a: Overall, reviews say it's peaceful and easy to sleep in, but rooms facing Petchkasem Road may pick up some noise from the main road · If you're a light sleeper, it's best to ask for a room that doesn't face the road, or a garden-view room, when you book · And brace yourself for the bed, which many reviews call quite firm.

faq.q: How do you get around for sightseeing from Wanarom Residence Hotel?
faq.a: This location needs a car to get around, because there's no motorbike rental or restaurants to walk to nearby · It's best to rent a car and drive yourself (there's free parking), call a Grab/taxi, or ask the property about transfers · From here it's about 10–15 minutes to drive into Krabi town, about 8–10 minutes to Wat Tham Suea, and an easy onward trip to Ao Nang or the piers for the islands.
